messages:
maria: Heads-up: canary from last night shows a small-request latency tail increase after the micro-lane packing changes. p50 up ~12ms, p95 up ~30ms for seq<=24. Not huge but reproducible.

raj: Saw that too. The telemetry traces point to additional pathing when a request races for a micro-lane vs joining an existing coalesce window. There's an extra compare-and-scan in the hot path.

lee: That scan was to allow cross-tenant micro-coalesce without creating a dedicated tiny lane. It improved packing on medium workloads but seems to penalize ultra-short requests.

devon: The tradeoff: packability vs fastpath simplicity. We optimized for token efficiency but the CPU path added ~8-10ms under lock contention.

maria: Can we emulate an experiment that isolates the two effects? e.g., enable micro-coalesce only when batch occupancy <= N or when request has warm KV flag.

raj: We can. I propose an experiment matrix: 
- A: micro-coalesce always (baseline canary)
- B: micro-coalesce gated by occupancy <=3
- C: micro-coalesce gated by kv_cache_hit=true
- D: dedicated micro-lane (non-coalescing) for seq<=24
We collect p50/p95/p99 + kv cache hit rate + allocation CPU ms.

devon: Also add a small admission API tweak: let callers pass deadline_hint_ms and a preference flag prefer_fastpath=true. Scheduler then fast-fails the coalesce_scan if prefer_fastpath and deadline_hint < 10ms. That avoids probe penalty.

lee: That keeps the runtime API minimal. But we must be careful: prefer_fastpath could be abused by tenants and hurt packing. Maybe expose per-tenant budget for prefer_fastpath tokens.

maria: Good call. We should have quota for fastpath requests per-tenant per-minute. Add telemetry: fastpath_quota_utilization.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout triggered for pool-canary-3 at 04:10 UTC. Monitoring thresholds: p50 delta <=10ms, p95 delta <=25ms.

raj: Implementation notes: temp flag micro_coalesce.gate = {type: "occupancy", threshold: 3} and a per-pool descriptor field reserved_slots_for_micro_lane to avoid coalescer double-counting.

devon: Example config I hacked: 
```
scheduler: {
  micro_coalesce: {
    enabled: true,
    gate: { type: "occupancy", threshold: 3 },
    max_seq: 24
  },
  lanes: {
    micro_lane: { enabled: false, reserved_slots: 0 }
  }
}
```

maria: For the canary let's run A/B across pools with B and C variants. Don't touch dedicated pools. Run for 24h and gather per-tenant histograms.

lee: Measurement detail: tag each request with lane_id, coalesce_join=true/false, kv_cache_hit=true/false, prefer_fastpath flag. We'll need to update the trace schema.

raj: On the scheduler side we'll expose metrics: scheduler.micro_coalesce.scan_time_ms, scheduler.micro_lane.reserved_slots, scheduler.fastpath.deadline_fastfail_count.

devon: Quick mitigation if regressions persist: short-circuit the scan when contention_count > X and fallback to baseline fastpath. That keeps packing benefits for quiet pools.

maria: Decision timeline: raj+devon implement metrics + API hooks today, lee config canary variants, run 24h, sync tomorrow to decide between gating vs dedicated micro-lane. Sasha should be looped in for the documentation update.

infra-bot: alert-bot: Canary pool-canary-3 p95 breached threshold at 06:03 UTC, automated rollback initiated.

maria: Rollback confirmed. Next step: deploy B and C across 10% pools each, leave control on 80% to compare. Keep dedicated micro-lane disabled.

lee: I'll draft the follow-up RFC fragment capturing the tradeoffs: "latency overhead from scan vs gains in token packing; KV-cache locality impact; admission surface complexity; per-tenant fastpath budgeting."

devon: Add microbench for the scan path in isolation (single-threaded) to quantify CPU cost per-request; that will help set thresholds.

raj: I'll wire up the telemetry and the quota enforcement in the admission layer.

maria: Thanks all. Keep messages short in the RFC draft; include the experiment matrix and expected metrics. We'll reconvene after 24h of canary data.
